newsitem.title: USA: USDA has $96.6 mln to aid farmers hurt by Fran.
newsitem.headline: USDA has $96.6 mln to aid farmers hurt by Fran.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Wednesday said it has $96.6 million in additional emergency funds to help farmers and local governments repair damage from Hurricane Fran and other natural disasters.
USDA said President Clinton signed legislation earlier this week that provided the additional monies.
USDA said of $63 million in new funding for its Emergency Watershed Protection Program, nearly $20 million will be used to repair damages in North Carolina, Maryland, Virginia, and West Virginia.
The National Forest Service will receive $8.6 million to repair damages caused by hurricanes on National Forest lands.
USDA said $25 million will be available to help producers rehabilitate farmland damaged by natural disasters and for carrying out water conservation during severe droughts.

USDA noted that in addition to the new funding, crop insurance has already paid $3 million in losses in North Carolina with claims expected to reach $91 million. These payments reflect losses from Hurricanes Bertha and Fran which hit many of the same counties twice.
Fran slammed the mid-Atlantic seaboard in early September, following on the heels of Hurricane Bertha in July.
